versions.summary: The first version: every starter as ZDD 0.13 ran it from the engine, so an upgrade that copies them in proves the records unchanged.
The schema and query readers ship with every bug known when the library began fixed. A repo that copied 0.1.0 is offered these; a new repo gets them from the start.

fixes.what: A foreign key added after the table is read: by ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT … FOREIGN KEY or ADD FOREIGN KEY, at table level, with no column list (the referenced table's primary key), or in a DO block that runs it outright or guards it on that constraint or table. DROP CONSTRAINT takes one away, by the name given or the name Postgres gave it, through renames. A column in a second key keeps it in an optional alsoReferences, beside references; a dropped column takes its whole key.
fixes.who: A repo whose migrations add foreign keys after CREATE TABLE, or inside a DO block. Its column records gain the references, and the tables gain the edges between them.
fixes.moves: No record id moves. Column records change: references (which may now name a table with no column) and alsoReferences.

fixes.what: A renamed table keeps the schema it was written with, public too: ALTER TABLE public.x RENAME TO y makes public.y, not y.
fixes.who: A repo whose migrations rename a schema-qualified table. Code that named the renamed table with its schema lost its data-access records with no warning; they arrive.
fixes.moves: The renamed table's id gains its schema: table:<namespace>/y becomes table:<namespace>/public.y. Repoint map links and blessings by the new record's renamedFrom.

fixes.what: f and public.f are one function, in every statement that names it.
fixes.who: A repo whose migrations name one function both with and without public.
fixes.moves: Where two function records were made, one remains: the id as first written. Repoint links to the other id at it.

fixes.what: UPDATE and DELETE on storage.buckets apply, or are reported when wider than one bucket; an INSERT of several buckets makes them all; its ON CONFLICT decides what a bucket already there does; a bucket's id and name are held apart, quoting read.
fixes.who: A repo that creates buckets with one INSERT of several rows, or changes or removes them in a later migration. Bucket records gain, lose or change.
fixes.moves: A bucket removed by a later DELETE loses its record; one made in a multi-row INSERT gains one.

fixes.what: UNIQUE(a, b) with no space is a constraint, never a column; a type changed USING an expression is the type alone; a CREATE TABLE over a table that is there is reported as unread.
fixes.who: A repo with any of those statements. A junk column disappears, a column type is corrected, or an item appears in the unread report to answer.

fixes.what: A table is referred to by its bare name, PUBLIC folded, so code that writes public.x reaches the table in either spelling.
fixes.who: A repo whose SQLAlchemy code qualifies table names with public, or whose schema reader writes them qualified. Data-access records arrive where they were missing.
fixes.moves: No record id moves. Data-access records are added, and routes gain the edges to their tables.

versions.summary: A Next.js screen takes the calls of the components and modules its page and layout import, as a React Router screen already did.

fixes.what: A surface takes the refs of the local modules its page or layout file imports, relative or @/, one hop away: their API calls, and the code it runs there, which a data-access adapter reads. A named import narrows the module to what the names reach; a default or namespace import takes it whole, with a note. Before, a page that rendered a component from outside appDir got none of its links, though its resource named the component.
fixes.who: A Next.js repo whose pages or layouts render components, or call helpers, from outside appDir. Their surfaces gain links to routes and tables, so a screen the map's gap check called "reaches nothing" may now reach them: its gaps.known or gaps.fine mark goes stale and lint warns until it is removed.
fixes.moves: No record id moves. Surface records gain refs, and the screens gain edges to what those modules reach.
